segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: At that last supper, knowing he was about to leave the world, Jesus did something no master would ever do for his servants.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He got up from the table, wrapped a towel around his waist, and poured water into a basin.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And he began to wash his disciples' feet — one by one.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: When he came to Peter, Peter pulled back.

segments.speaker: scripture
segments.text: Thou shalt never wash my feet.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: You will never wash my feet, Peter said. Not you. Not for me. And Jesus answered him gently, but he did not back down.

segments.speaker: jesus
segments.text: If I wash thee not, thou hast no part with me.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: That is how serious this is. Peter thought he was protecting Jesus's dignity. What he was really doing was refusing to be loved.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: When he had finished, he dried their feet with the towel at his waist, sat back down, and asked if they understood what he had just done.

segments.speaker: jesus
segments.text: If I then, your Lord and Master, have washed your feet; ye also ought to wash one another's feet.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: If I, your Lord and your Teacher, have washed your feet, he said, then you ought to wash each other's. Whatever he just did for them, they were to go do for each other.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The greatest one in the room knelt at the dirtiest job in the house. That is the kind of king he is.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He kneels to serve the ones he loves. Will you let him near enough to do it for you?
